title: Count Dominant Indices
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, count the indices i where nums[i] exceeds the average of the subsequent elements.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, count the indices i where nums[i] exceeds the average of the subsequent elements. The average is calculated by summing the elements from nums[i+1] to nums[n-1] and dividing by their count. Exclude the rightmost element from being considered dominant.
constraints: An index before the last is dominant when its value is greater than the average of all following values.
Do not count the final index.
Return the number of dominant indices.
hints: Maintain the sum of elements strictly after i.
Avoid floating point by comparing nums[i]*suffix_count with suffix_sum.
Stop before the final index because its suffix is empty.
editorial: Stop before the final index because its suffix is empty.

tests.explanation: Five exceeds the following average 3.5 and four exceeds three, so both indices count.
Neither earlier value exceeds its following average.
